memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'"If the anointed priest sins, bringing guilt on the people, he must bring to the LORD a young bull without defect as a sin offering for the sin he has committed."'" - Lev 4:3 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God begins with the priest. Not the ordinary Israelite, not even the community — the man at the front.

And notice the sobering phrase: bringing guilt on the people. When the high priest sinned, the whole nation was affected. His failure did not stay in his own house. Leadership magnifies consequence.

Notice also that his offering is the largest in the chapter — a young bull, the most costly animal. God does not go easier on the spiritual leader. If anything, more is required.

This cuts two ways for us. If you lead anything — a church, a family, a team, a small group — your failures land on people who trust you. That should make you careful, not paralysed. James warns that those who teach will be judged more strictly (Jas 3:1).

And if you have been wounded by a leader's failure, this verse tells you God is not indifferent. He addressed it first, before anything else in the chapter.

But there is hope here too. The high priest of Israel needed a sacrifice for himself. Hebrews makes the contrast: we have a High Priest who is holy, blameless, pure, who does not need to offer sacrifices for his own sins (Heb 7:26-27). Every human leader will disappoint. Christ never will.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where does my example affect others more than I realise?
2. Have I placed expectations on a human leader that only Christ can bear?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, guard those who lead Your people, and guard me in whatever influence You have given me. Thank You for a High Priest who never fails. Amen.
